task.question: What institution produced data suggesting over 2,700 deaths due to heatwaves in the United Kingdom in 2026?
task.evidence: 2026 United Kingdom heatwaves: Data produced by Imperial College London, the Met Office and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine suggests that more than 2,700 deaths may have occurred as a result of the heatwaves in May and June.

answer:
The data suggesting over 2,700 deaths due to heatwaves in the United Kingdom in 2026 was produced by researchers from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), Imperial College London, and the Met Office. 

FINAL: LSHTM, Imperial College London, Met Office

[More than 2,700 excess deaths estimated in England and Wales during May and June] https://phys.org/news/2026-07-excess-deaths-england-wales-june.html More than 2,700 people are estimated to have died from heat-related causes during the record-breaking May and June 2026 heat waves in England and Wales, according to a new rapid analysis report led by researchers from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), Imperial College London and the Met Office. The analysis suggests that around 42% of these deaths were due to the additional heat caused by human-induced climate change. [...] Record-breaking May–June 2026 heat waves in England and Wales were linked to an estimated >2,700 heat-related excess deaths, about 550 in May and 2,200 in June. Human-induced climate change contributed ~42% of these deaths, with daytime maxima 3–4°C higher than without warming. Mortality was highest in older adults and in southern and midland regions, underscoring rising early-summer heat-health risks and the need for adaptation. [...] Researchers estimate that about 550 heat-related deaths occurred in England and Wales during the May heat wave, which took place May 21–29, 2026, and about 2,200 during the June heat wave, from June 18 to 28, 2026.
